deviations: s12-26 removes one symbol the ledger did not name. Deleting createTemplate left 'INVALID_TEMPLATE' with no producer anywhere in src — its TSDoc defined it as what createTemplate throws — so the union member and its INTERPRET_ERROR_CODES entry went with it, on the same reasoning s12-39 applies to INTERPRET_ID. breaking-radius.json records no external consumer for s12-26, and grep finds no reference to the code outside the deleted call site. If the Orchestrator wants the code retained, the restore is three lines plus a guide row.

s12-37 removes deriveAggregateField, which the ledger did not name. Its only consumer was the deleted aggregate emission, and its documented purpose ('the aggregate suffix Sum/Count/Average/Minimum/Maximum') was that emission; nothing else in src, tests or the fleet radius calls it. Its guide row, fence lines and tests went with it.

s12-37's binding mechanism is my reading of 'bind through the existing Template.computations'. resolveExpression takes Record<string, number> and @orkestrel/reason's applyOperation is scalar, so an array-valued entity could not reach a computation at all. Clarifier#resolveComputations therefore binds each numeric element under {field}.{index} — the same dotted addressing FieldPath already uses — and the integration test drives the first real consumer end to end (a declared 'total' computation summing value.0 + value.1 + value.2). No aggregate-name list was introduced.

s12-35 has one half no test can drive. The teardown of a context the orchestrator constructed itself has no public observer, because Interpret publishes no context accessor. Rather than write a test whose name overclaims what its assertions check, the gap is recorded as a comment beside the supplied-context test in tests/src/core/Interpret.test.ts.

README.md carries an edit beyond a pure rename: its Usage fence built the orchestrator with a hand-rolled { extract: () => … } stage stub. That is the s12-47 finding, whose repair already landed in the guide and in the createInterpret example, and the README is the copy the campaign missed; the fence now uses createExtractor, matching them.
